The circles $r=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ and $r=\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ intersect at points $O$ and $A,$ as shown above. What are the polar coordinates of the point $A?$
question.worked_solution:
First of all, we notice from the graph that the origin $O$ is an obvious first point of intersection.

To find the second point of intersection, we set the equations of the curves equal to each other and solve for $\theta :$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta ) \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the solution $\theta ={60}^{∘}$ in the $1$st quadrant.

Now, we use the equation $r=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ to find the $r$-coordinate of the point $A:$  

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =3\operatorname{cos}⁡({60}^{∘}) \\  & =3\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polar coordinates of the point $A$ are 

$\,$ $(r,\theta )=(\frac{3}{2},{60}^{∘}).$
